policy.authority: Operational metadata only. GitHub issues, PRs and commit evidence remain authoritative. Never merge this branch or store canon, credentials, transcripts or uncommitted private content.
policy.write: Fetch file from this exact branch and use returned blob SHA with GitHub update_file. On conflict or timeout reread; never blind-retry. Preserve other lanes. New claim requires fresh eligibility check, no live reservation in repository, unique owner/operation ID, generation increment, 45-minute lease. Before any consequential write check current ownership, lease and target branch SHA; release promptly. This is cooperative, not an enforcement gate for external tools. Use the incremented registry revision as generation (monotonically increasing even after release). Refresh lease during long work; do not proceed after losing ownership. Repository-wide lease serializes participating writers only. Use real UTC timestamps; do not hold leases while merely reading or waiting on a dependency.
policy.recovery: Inspect only current checkpoint and changed evidence. Check actual Issue/PR state, HEAD/base and dependencies. Resume only if useful, authorized and compatible; blocked/stale/resolved/cancelled tasks are not retried by default. After two attempts with no material progress mark blocked with reason; reopen only on new evidence. No automatic merge/deploy or expansion of permissions. States: available, active, recoverable, blocked, obsolete, cancelled, completed. A terminal state is not a candidate. For a blocked task, require a changed dependency or materially new evidence. Do not reopen a completed/obsolete/cancelled task; create a new task only if a distinct current objective warrants it.
policy.checkpoint: Persist after claim, first useful evidence and each material milestone before further risky work. Keep objective, acceptance, issue/PR, branch, base/head SHA, evidence, completed, pending, next action, blocker, session/operation ID and progress counters. A completed checkpoint requires actual evidence meeting acceptance. Store references, not copied logs. Release on completion/pause. An expired lease permits revalidation and new generation, not blind continuation. Keep only the latest task per lane in this file; before replacement preserve evidence in the relevant Issue/PR or Git history. Never change policy/schema during ordinary checkpoint updates.
